title: Prime-chain length versus valuation rational rank
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $A$ be a valuation ring of $K$, i.e. a subring $A\subseteq K$ such that for every $a\in K^\times$ at least one of $a,a^{-1}$ lies in $A$; write $A^\times$ for its unit group. Put $\Gamma=K^\times/A^\times$ and $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma)=\dim_{\mathbf Q}(\Gamma\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q)\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$. If $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\dots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ are prime ideals of $A$, then $n\le\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma)$.

source.place: §2.1, Lemma 2.1.2 (Abhyankar inequality) and Corollary 2.1.3(i) for the height consequence; the local document copy is unavailable.

proof.text: The quotient $\Gamma=K^\times/A^\times$ carries the total order $[x]\le[y]$ exactly when $y/x\in A$: the valuation-ring alternative applied to $y/x$ gives comparability, and multiplication by a representative preserves the relation. The quotient is well defined because multiplying $x$ or $y$ by units does not change membership in $A$.

source.place: §2.1, p. 7, the quotient-order construction and the valuation-ring/value-group setup; checked in the author’s v3 PDF online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-prime-convex-correspondence] to the given valuation ring. Its canonical order anti-isomorphism sends the strict prime chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ to a strict chain of $n$ convex subgroups of $\Gamma$.

source.place: §2.1, p. 7, lines 401–416: overrings, points of Spec, and convex subgroups of the value group; checked in the author’s v3 PDF online.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-convex-chain-rational-rank], every strict chain of $n$ convex subgroups of $\Gamma$ has $n\le\dim_{\mathbf Q}(\Gamma\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q)=\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma)$. This is the required inequality.

source.place: §2.1, pp. 7–8, the convex-subgroup/height discussion together with Lemma 2.1.2 and Corollary 2.1.3(i); the ordered-group chain bound is the stated convex-rank consequence, checked in the author’s v3 PDF online.

proof_origin.place: §2.1, pp. 7–8, including the valuation-ring/value-group correspondence, Lemma 2.1.2 and Corollary 2.1.3(i); checked in the author’s v3 PDF online.
